title: ISBD punctuation master rules
content_markdown:
# 2\. ISBD Prescribed Punctuation — Master Rules

ISBD punctuation substitutes for labelled fields: the mark itself tells the reader what kind of data follows\. Two conventions are constant \(ISBD, General Introduction, 0\.4; also stated in AACR2 1\.0C\):

- Every prescribed mark, other than the comma and full stop, is preceded and followed by a single space, e\.g\. ' : ', ' / ', ' ; ', ' = ', ' \+ '\. A mark that begins a new area \(' \. — '\) keeps its own spacing; a mark occurring at the very start of a field is not preceded by a space\.
- The prescribed punctuation is given in ADDITION to normal grammatical punctuation of the data itself; it is not a substitute for it \(AACR2 1\.0C1\)\.

## 2\.1 Mark\-by\-Mark Rule Table

__Mark__

__Used for__

__Rule__

__Governing source__

__Example\(s\)__

\. — 

Area separator

Introduces a new ISBD area \(Edition, Publication, Physical Description, Series\) when a record is displayed as a single run\-on paragraph\.

ISBD 0\.4; AACR2 1\.0C1

… 12th ed\. — Cambridge :

 : 

Other title information; publisher's name

Follows title proper \(before subtitle, MARC 245$a→$b\) and follows place of publication \(before publisher, 260$a→$b\)\.

ISBD Area 1 & 4; AACR2 1\.1B1, 1\.4C1

Cambridge : Cambridge University Press,

 / 

First statement of responsibility

Separates title from who is responsible for the work \(245$a/$b → 245$c\)\.

ISBD Area 1; AACR2 1\.1F1

… survive / by Conor Gearty\.

 ; 

\(a\) additional statement of responsibility of a DIFFERENT function; \(b\) dimensions after other physical details; \(c\) volume/number in a series

Repeatable once per additional element of a different kind\.

ISBD Area 1, 5, 6; AACR2 1\.1F5, 1\.5D1, 1\.6

by A ; translated by B  /  ill\. ; 24 cm  /  \(series ; 12\)

 , 

\(a\) after publisher, before date; \(b\) between co\-responsible names of the SAME function when the title page itself uses a comma

No space before, one space after\.

ISBD Area 4; AACR2 1\.4D1, 1\.1F5

Cambridge University Press, 2006\.

 \. 

Ends a completed ISBD area; ends abbreviations \(ed\., p\., cm\.\); ends a sentence\-style note

No space before the mark\.

ISBD General rules; AACR2 1\.0C1

12th ed\.   Includes index\.

 = 

Parallel title or parallel statement in another language

Only when the source itself gives a title in more than one language\.

ISBD Area 1; AACR2 1\.1D1

Title = Titre parallèle

 \+ 

Accompanying material note

Placed at the very end of the physical description area \(300$e\)\.

ISBD Area 5; AACR2 1\.5E1

174 p\. ; 24 cm\. \+ 1 CD

 \( \) 

Encloses the whole series statement; also a fuller form of name and the GMD

No internal space after '\(' or before '\)'\.

ISBD Area 6; AACR2 1\.6, 22\.18, 1\.1C

\(Hamlyn lectures ; 12\)

 \[ \] 

Encloses any data supplied by the cataloguer that is not printed on the item

Never present inferred data as if it were on the piece — brackets are mandatory\.

ISBD 0\.4, A\.3; AACR2 1\.1F7, 1\.4C6

\[S\.l\. : s\.n\., 2006?\]

 — 

Separates successive subdivisions in a subject heading string \(600/610/650 $x/$y/$z\)

Not an ISBD area mark; a subject\-heading convention \(LCSH/Sears\)\.

LC Subject Headings Manual; MARC 21 6XX

Human rights — India — 21st century

title: Statement of responsibility (245$c) scenarios
content_markdown:
# 3\. Statement of Responsibility — MARC 245 $c \(Comprehensive Rules\)

The statement of responsibility identifies the person\(s\) or body/bodies responsible for the intellectual/artistic content of the work, and their role\. It is transcribed from the chief source of information \(the title page for a book\), NOT composed or normalised by the cataloguer, except where AACR2 explicitly instructs an abbreviation or omission\.

*Source: AACR2 1\.1F1–1\.1F15 \(Statements of responsibility\); ISBD Area 1 \(Title and Statement of Responsibility Area, punctuation 1\.4\.5\); MARC 21 Bibliographic, field 245 subfield $c\.*

## 3\.1 General Rule and Basic Punctuation

- Transcribe the statement of responsibility exactly as it appears on the title page, in the order and form given, including the linking word \('by', 'edited by', 'with an introduction by'\)\. — AACR2 1\.1F1\.
- The FIRST statement of responsibility is introduced by a space\-slash\-space ' / ' immediately after the title \(or subtitle\)\. — ISBD 1\.4\.5\.1; AACR2 1\.1F1\.
- Names of two or three persons/bodies performing the SAME function are recorded together, separated exactly as they appear on the source \(usually a comma, with 'and' before the last name if the title page uses it\)\. No semicolon is used between names of the same function\. — AACR2 1\.1F5\.
- A subsequent statement of responsibility that names a person/body performing a DIFFERENT function is introduced by a space\-semicolon\-space ' ; '\. — AACR2 1\.1F11; ISBD 1\.4\.5\.2\.
- The whole statement of responsibility area ends with a full stop, unless another ISBD area follows immediately without a break \(in which case that area's own leading punctuation is used\)\.

## 3\.2 Scenario\-by\-Scenario Rules

### \(a\) Single author

Transcribe the name exactly as given, preceded by 'by' if that word appears on the title page \(do not add 'by' if the title page omits it, unless required for sense — AACR2 1\.1F1\)\.

__245$c: __*by Conor Gearty\.*

- If the personal author's name is already the 100 main entry, still repeat it in 245$c exactly as printed \(245$c is a transcription field, independent of the 100 heading form\)\.

### \(b\) Two authors \(same function\)

Both names are recorded in a single statement, in the order given on the title page, joined exactly as printed — usually 'and' or an ampersand if that is what appears\.

__245$c: __*by John Smith and Mary Jones\.*

- Do NOT insert a semicolon between two co\-authors — a semicolon is reserved for a change of function \(AACR2 1\.1F5 vs 1\.1F11\)\.

### \(c\) Three authors \(same function\)

All three are named, in title\-page order, following the title page's own punctuation \(commas between the first two, 'and' before the last\)\.

__245$c: __*by John Smith, Mary Jones, and David Lee\.*

- AACR2 1\.1F5 permits recording up to three names of a single function in full; a fourth or more triggers the 'et al\.' rule below\.

### \(d\) One editor

Recorded with the phrase actually printed on the title page — commonly 'edited by'\.

__245$c: __*edited by Anita Sharma\.*

- If the whole work is essentially an edited compilation with no single 'author', the editor statement still goes in 245$c; whether the editor becomes a MAIN entry \(100\) or an ADDED entry \(700\) depends on AACR2 21\.1 \(see Section 5\)\.

### \(e\) Multiple editors

Treated exactly like multiple authors of the same function — names joined as printed, up to three in full, four or more truncated with '\[et al\.\]'\.

__245$c \(two editors\): __*edited by Anita Sharma and Rakesh Kumar\.*

__245$c \(four\+ editors\): __*edited by Anita Sharma \[et al\.\]\.*

### \(f\) One or more translators

A translator performs a DIFFERENT function from the author, so the translator's statement is always introduced by a semicolon, even if there is only one author before it\.

__245$c: __*by Gabriel García Márquez ; translated by Gregory Rabassa\.*

- Multiple translators of equal function are joined with 'and'/comma exactly like multiple authors, still preceded by a single semicolon before the group\.

__245$c \(two translators\): __*by Haruki Murakami ; translated by Jay Rubin and Philip Gabriel\.*

*Source: AACR2 1\.1F11 \(statements of different responsibility linked by semicolon\); ISBD 1\.4\.5\.2\.*

### \(g\) Illustrators

An illustrator is a different function from the author/editor/translator and is therefore also introduced by a semicolon\.

__245$c: __*by Roald Dahl ; illustrated by Quentin Blake\.*

- If BOTH a translator and an illustrator are present, each different function gets its own semicolon\-introduced clause, in the order they appear on the title page \(commonly: author ; translator ; illustrator\)\.

__245$c \(author \+ translator \+ illustrator\): __*by Antoine de Saint\-Exupéry ; translated by Katherine Woods ; illustrated by the author\.*

### \(h\) Compilers

Used for anthologies, bibliographies, or works assembled from multiple sources; the phrase 'compiled by' is transcribed as printed\.

__245$c: __*compiled by the Reference Department, Christ University Library\.*

- A compiler is treated as a distinct function; if a compiler follows a named author/editor of the individual pieces, separate with a semicolon\.

### \(i\) Organization / corporate body as author

Transcribe the corporate name exactly as printed, following whatever introductory wording is used \('by', 'prepared by', 'issued by'\)\.

__245$c: __*prepared by the World Health Organization\.*

- Whether the corporate body becomes the 110 MAIN entry or a 710 ADDED entry depends on the AACR2 21\.1B corporate\-responsibility test \(see Section 5\.2\) — this is independent of how 245$c is transcribed, which is always a literal transcription\.

### \(j\) Combinations — multiple authors with translator\(s\) and illustrator\(s\)

Build the statement left to right exactly as the title page presents it: co\-authors/co\-editors of the SAME function are grouped and joined with commas/'and'; each new, DIFFERENT function starts a new semicolon\-led clause\.

__245$c: __*by Chinua Achebe and Wole Soyinka ; translated by Jane Doe ; illustrated by Ben Okafor \[et al\.\]\.*

- Read the title page top\-to\-bottom / left\-to\-right to determine the printed order; do not reorder alphabetically or by perceived importance \(AACR2 1\.1F1, 1\.1F3\)\.

### \(k\) Other common responsibility statements

__Scenario__

__Rule__

__Example__

Foreword/introduction by a different person

Add as its own semicolon\-clause, since it is a distinct contribution\.

by Jane Austen ; with an introduction by Fay Weldon\.

General editor / series editor named on a series volume

Recorded in 245$c if on the title page of THIS volume; otherwise recorded in the series statement \(440/490\), not 245$c\.

by A\. Author ; general editor, B\. Editor\.

'With contributions by…'

Treated as a distinct function; semicolon\-introduced, names joined as printed\.

by Lead Author ; with contributions by Jane Roe and John Poe\.

Revised/updated by a person other than the original author

Recorded as its own clause; often combined with an edition statement in 250 as well\.

by Original Author ; revised by New Editor\.

Statement not on title page but found elsewhere in the item

Supply in square brackets if considered important; otherwise give in a 500 note\.

by \[Anonymous, identified on t\.p\. verso as John Doe\]\.

Pseudonym or pen name only given

Transcribe the pseudonym as printed in 245$c; the real name \(if known\) goes in the 100 heading with the pseudonym as a 400/reference, not altered in 245$c\.

by Currer Bell\.

## 3\.3 Statement of Responsibility — Punctuation Quick Reference

__Situation__

__Punctuation rule__

__Example__

Same function, 2–3 names

Comma / 'and' exactly as printed — NO semicolon

by A, B, and C\.

4\+ names, same function

Name first only \+ ' \[et al\.\]'

by A \[et al\.\]\.

Change of function

Semicolon before the new clause

by A ; translated by B

Several different functions in sequence

One semicolon before EACH new function group

by A ; translated by B ; illustrated by C

Statement supplied by cataloguer, not on the source

Enclose the supplied words in square brackets

\[compiled by\] the editors

End of the whole 245 field \(no further ISBD area follows on the same line\)

Full stop

… illustrated by C\.

## 3\.4 Common Mistakes in 245 $c

- Using a semicolon between two co\-authors of the same function \(should be a comma/'and'\)\.
- Forgetting the semicolon before a translator/illustrator/editor when their function differs from the preceding name \(a very common KOHA data\-entry error\)\.
- Alphabetising or reordering names instead of following the exact title\-page sequence\.
- Writing 'et al\.' without square brackets — it MUST be bracketed because it is a cataloguer addition, not printed text \(AACR2 1\.1F5\)\.
- Adding academic titles/degrees \(Dr\., PhD, Prof\.\) that are not required to identify the person — AACR2 1\.1F7 says omit titles of honour/degree unless needed for identification or grammatical sense\.
- Typing the statement of responsibility into 245$a \(title\) instead of 245$c — the statement of responsibility is always its own subfield\.
- Confusing 245$c \(literal transcription\) with the 700 added\-entry decision — every person recorded in 245$c who is not the 100 main entry should normally get a 700 added entry, but the WORDING of 245$c is never changed to match 700's normalised name form\.

title: AACR2 main/added entry choice rules
content_markdown:
# 5\. Choice and Form of Main/Added Entry \(AACR2 Chapter 21\)

This governs WHICH heading becomes the 1XX main entry versus a 7XX added entry — a decision made independently of, and prior to, filling in 245$c\.

## 5\.1 The General Rule

- A work by a single personal author is entered under that person \(100\)\. — AACR2 21\.1A1
- A work of shared responsibility by up to three persons/bodies performing the same function is entered under the FIRST named, with the others as 700/710 added entries\. — AACR2 21\.6B
- A work by four or more persons/bodies of the same function, with no principal author indicated, is entered under TITLE \(no 100\), with an added entry \(700\) for the first\-named person only, unless local policy adds more\. — AACR2 21\.6C1
- A work of MIXED responsibility \(e\.g\. one person writes, a different person illustrates or translates\) is entered under whichever person is chiefly responsible for the content that gives the work its character — commonly the original author, not the translator/illustrator/editor\. — AACR2 21\.8–21\.20 \(mixed responsibility rules by work type\)

## 5\.2 Corporate Body Main Entry Test

A corporate body becomes the 110 MAIN entry only if the work falls into one of the specific categories in AACR2 21\.1B2:

- \(a\) Administrative works about the body itself \(annual reports, directories, internal policy\)\.
- \(b\) Legal, governmental or religious works of the type the body is legally empowered to issue \(laws, decrees, treaties, liturgies\)\.
- \(c\) Works recording the COLLECTIVE thought of the body \(official statements, position papers\)\.
- \(d\) Reports of the collective ACTIVITY of a conference, expedition, or event \(proceedings, results\)\.
- \(e\) Sound recordings, films or broadcasts where the body is the performing/producing entity\.
- \(f\) Certain cartographic works produced by the body\.

Publication or sponsorship by a corporate body, on its own, is NEVER sufficient for a 110 main entry \(AACR2 21\.1B3\) — such a body is recorded instead as a 710 added entry, and the work is entered under its personal author or title\.

## 5\.3 Quick Decision Table

__Situation__

__Access point decision__

__Rule cited__

Single personal author

100 = that author

AACR2 21\.1A1

2–3 co\-authors, same function

100 = first named; 700 = others

AACR2 21\.6B

4\+ co\-authors/contributors, same function, no principal author stated

No 100; entry under title \(245\); 700 = first named only

AACR2 21\.6C1

Corporate body meets 21\.1B2 categories

110 = that body

AACR2 21\.1B2

Corporate body is merely publisher/sponsor

No 110; entry under author/title; 710 = the body

AACR2 21\.1B3

Named conference/meeting issuing its own proceedings

111 = the meeting

AACR2 21\.1B2\(d\)

Editor of an anthology of many authors' works

No 100 for the editor; entry under title; 700 = editor

AACR2 21\.7B

Translation, original author identifiable and dominant

100 = original author; 700 = translator

AACR2 21\.14 / 21\.6
